_about: Reachability dispositions for the advisories of `pnpm audit --prod --json` over website 983681c, authored by the security review. Keys: a module name sets the default for every advisory of that module; `module|GHSA` overrides it; `module@version-prefix` overrides it for one installed version line. disp: REACHED | CONDITIONAL | ABSENT | HOST | BUILD | UNLOADED | DEV. ships: server | browser | both | build | none.

@babel/runtime.how: Bundled through @hello-pangea/color-picker, which imports only the helpers defineProperty and extends; the advisory's named-capture-group regex helper is not imported.

@smithy/config-resolver.how: The S3 client's region is the literal 'us-east-1' in previewBucket.ts getS3; no request input reaches it.

baseline-browser-mapping.how: Browser-support data Next reads while building; its input is the repository's own configuration.

brace-expansion.how: Installed under project-utils > prisma-kysely, a Prisma code generator. project-utils' committed dist requires only pg, kysely, zod and its own files, so the generator chain is never loaded by the website.

minimatch.how: Same generator chain as brace-expansion (project-utils > prisma-kysely > @prisma/internals); never loaded by the website.

tmp.how: Same generator chain as brace-expansion (project-utils > prisma-kysely > @prisma/internals); never loaded by the website.

uuid.how: The AWS retry middleware calls v4() with no buffer argument; the advisory needs v3, v5 or v6 with a caller-supplied buffer. The second copy sits in the unloaded Prisma generator chain.

braces.how: Under @headlessui/tailwindcss > tailwindcss > chokidar: Tailwind's file watcher, run only while building, over the repository's own files.

micromatch.how: Under tailwindcss: glob matching of the repository's own content paths at build time.

picomatch.how: Under tailwindcss > chokidar > anymatch: build-time glob matching of the repository's own paths.

postcss.how: Tailwind's PostCSS, run at build time over the repository's own stylesheets; no visitor-supplied CSS is ever parsed.

postcss-selector-parser.how: Under tailwindcss: parses the repository's own selectors at build time.

source-map-js.how: Under tailwindcss > postcss: source maps of the repository's own stylesheets at build time.

yaml.how: Under tailwindcss > postcss-load-config: reads a PostCSS config file at build time; the repository's config is postcss.config.js.

diff.how: Under tailwindcss > postcss-load-config > ts-node: build tooling only.

nanoid.how: getUrlCode.ts calls customAlphabet(alphabet, 7): the size is the literal 7, and every advisory needs a caller-controlled size. Its one caller is the Redis share-code store.

nanoid@3.how: The 3.x copy belongs to Tailwind's PostCSS and runs only at build time, with fixed sizes.

cookie.how: next-auth serialises cookies whose names, paths and domains are fixed by its own configuration; no request input chooses them.

cross-spawn.how: Under @vercel/functions > @vercel/oidc > @vercel/cli-exec. The website imports only waitUntil, and the package's main entry does not load its oidc entry.

decode-uri-component.how: Providers.tsx getMessage passes the request header x-query-params to queryString.parse, which decodes with this package. Any client can send that header on a /message page; the middleware overwrites it only when the URL has a query string. Measured: see F-1.

fast-loops.how: Under react-use > nano-css > inline-style-prefixer. The react-use hooks the website imports (useLatest, useUpdateEffect, useLockBodyScroll, useClickAway and eight others) include none of the nano-css ones (useCss).

fast-xml-parser.how: The AWS SDK uses only XMLParser, over the object store's answers to ListObjects and DeleteObjects. The XML comes from the storage provider at CDN_ENDPOINT; an attacker would have to control that provider's responses. Object keys in a listing are built by the website from a message number and a generated nonce.

fast-xml-parser|GHSA-gh4j-gqv2-49f6.how: An XMLBuilder defect; the AWS SDK packages installed use XMLParser only, and the website does not import the package.

fast-xml-parser|GHSA-fj3w-jwp8-x2g3.how: An XMLBuilder defect; the AWS SDK packages installed use XMLParser only, and the website does not import the package.

form-data.how: bot/utils/DiscordMessage.ts builds a multipart form only when a file was attached with addFile, and addFile has no caller, so no form is ever constructed.

form-data@3.how: Installed under pusher > @types/node-fetch, a package of type declarations only; nothing executes it.

immutable.how: Under sass, which compiles the repository's own stylesheets at build time.

jose.how: The advisory needs a JWE that decrypts. next-auth here uses database sessions (an adapter, no JWT strategy); the only encrypted tokens are its own sign-in check cookies, which cannot be forged without the server secret.

js-cookie.how: The website calls only Cookies.get (CookieConsent.tsx, getClientSessionCookie.ts). The advisory needs an attributes object passed to set, remove, withAttributes or withConverter. The 2.2.1 copy belongs to react-use's useCookie, which is not imported.

kysely.how: The dialect is Postgres (project-utils postgres.js), and the website's only raw SQL is three sql template literals whose one interpolated value is a bound parameter. No sql.lit, no sql.raw, no JSON-path builder and no Kysely<any> outside a comment.

lodash.how: Bundled through @hello-pangea/color-picker, which imports debounce, each, isEqual and merge; the advisories concern template, unset, omit and pullAt.

next-auth|GHSA-7rqj-j65f-68wh.how: Needs the email (magic-link) provider. The only provider configured is Discord (src/server/auth.ts).

next-auth|GHSA-5jpx-9hw9-2fx4.how: Needs the email provider and nodemailer. The only provider configured is Discord.

next-auth|GHSA-xmf8-cvqr-rfgj.how: Needs the application to call getToken() itself. The website never calls it.

next-auth|GHSA-x445-f3h2-j279.how: Needs more than one OAuth provider with account linking. One provider is configured.

sanitize-html.how: Declared in package.json and imported nowhere. Its one mention is inside a commented-out block of JsonModalBody.tsx.

sharp.how: The website imports sharp nowhere. Next's own image optimiser uses the 0.34.5 copy, and that optimiser runs only when Next serves /_next/image itself; on Vercel the platform's image service answers that path. The directly declared 0.32.6 copy is used by nothing.

tar-fs.how: Used by sharp 0.32.6's installer to unpack its prebuilt binary during pnpm install. It never runs in a request, and the archive it unpacks comes from sharp's release host.

ws.how: The 8.13.0 copy is an optional peer of @vercel/functions, loaded by a dynamic import inside its websocket helper. The website calls only waitUntil.

ws@7.how: The 7.5.9 copy belongs to webpack-bundle-analyzer, which @next/bundle-analyzer requires only when ANALYZE=true on a webpack build.

zod.how: Every tRPC input is parsed with zod 3.22.4 on the server. A signed-in user can post a body of up to 1 MB to message.upsert whose array elements all fail. Measured: see F-2. (Also bundled in the browser, where a user can only slow their own tab.)

next|GHSA-2464-fhr4-w9xw.how: Image optimiser decoding an SVG with sharp below 0.35.5. Runs only where Next serves /_next/image itself. On Vercel the platform's image service answers that path. The advisory itself does not say whether managed hosting is affected; see A-1.

next|GHSA-2xp9-vwfh-vxw4.how: Image optimiser decoding an AVIF with libheif. Same position as the SVG advisory: self-hosted image optimisation only; the advisory is silent on managed hosting; see A-1.

next|GHSA-673q-mjm6-r5xr.how: Needs Cache Components and a `use cache` function returning typed arrays. The source has no `use cache` directive and next.config.js does not enable cacheComponents.

next|GHSA-p293-qw3h-jr36.how: Needs a server on a Windows filesystem. Vercel's functions run on Linux, and so does this box.

next|GHSA-267c-6grr-h53f.how: The site has a middleware and App Router pages, so its matcher can be skipped this way. The middleware authorises nothing: it only copies the path and query into two request headers. Skipping it exposes no protected content.

next|GHSA-26hh-7cqf-hhc6.how: The Turbopack follow-up to GHSA-267c-6grr-h53f; same position: the middleware can be skipped and authorises nothing.

next|GHSA-492v-c6pp-mqqv.how: A middleware bypass on dynamic routes. The middleware authorises nothing; access to a message is decided in the tRPC procedures.

next|GHSA-36qx-fr4f-26g5.how: Needs Pages Router pages with i18n. next.config.js has no i18n key, and the Pages Router holds API routes only.

next|GHSA-6gpp-xcg3-4w24.how: Needs i18n configured with a single locale. next.config.js has no i18n key.

next|GHSA-89xv-2m56-2m9x.how: Needs a Server Action that forwards or redirects, on a host that does not pin the Host header. The source has no `use server` directive.

next|GHSA-8h8q-6873-q5fj.how: The advisory names one precondition, the App Router, and the site's pages are App Router pages. A crafted request costs CPU while it is deserialised. Not exercised here: the advisory publishes no request; see F-3.

next|GHSA-q4gf-8mx6-v5v3.how: Same position as GHSA-8h8q-6873-q5fj: an App Router denial of service with no further precondition stated; see F-3.

next|GHSA-c4j6-fc7j-m34r.how: Self-hosted built-in Node server only; the advisory states Vercel-hosted deployments are not affected.

next|GHSA-cjq9-62q9-8jv4.how: Image optimiser fetching an allow-listed remote host whose DNS an attacker controls. The two allow-listed hosts are cdn.discordapp.com and cdn.jsdelivr.net, and the optimiser runs only where Next serves /_next/image itself.

next|GHSA-m99w-x7hq-7vfj.how: Needs at least one Server Action; the advisory states applications not using Server Actions are not vulnerable. The source has no `use server` directive.

next|GHSA-p3m5-59mp-jv5r.how: Needs at least one Server Action; the advisory states applications not using Server Actions are not vulnerable.

next|GHSA-mg66-mrh9-m8jx.how: Needs Cache Components (partial prerendering). Not enabled in next.config.js.

next|GHSA-p9j2-gv94-2wf4.how: Needs a rewrite or redirect whose destination hostname comes from the request. next.config.js has no rewrites, and its two redirects go to a fixed discord.gg address and to a path on the same site.

next|GHSA-3x4c-7xq6-9pq8.how: Unbounded image cache on disk; the advisory states platforms with their own image optimisation, such as Vercel, are not impacted.

next|GHSA-4633-3j49-mh5q.how: Needs a cached server-side fetch whose request body is in a non-UTF-8 charset. The App Router code fetches with GET only, and no fetch opts into caching.

next|GHSA-68g3-v927-f742.how: Needs fetch(new Request(init), aDifferentInit). The source constructs no Request.

next|GHSA-4c39-4ccg-62r3.how: Needs a Server Action on the Edge runtime. The source has no `use server` directive.

next|GHSA-4jqv-mc3x-m676.how: Self-hosted Pages Router static pages; the advisory states Vercel deployments are not affected, and the Pages Router here holds API routes only.

next|GHSA-7qx7-33qx-rqx2.how: Self-hosted image optimiser accepting an SVG it should refuse; the advisory scopes it to self-hosted deployments.

next|GHSA-955p-x3mx-jcvp.how: Discloses Server Action and `use cache` endpoint identifiers. The source has neither.

next|GHSA-f3mh-rxg3-f5g2.how: Needs an Edge runtime route that sets a cookie through NextResponse. The one Edge route, interactions-edge, sets no cookie.

next|GHSA-f87g-xv8r-7p7x.how: Needs App Router metadata image routes (opengraph-image, twitter-image). The source has none.

next|GHSA-ffhc-5mcf-pf4q.how: Needs an application that relies on CSP nonces behind a shared cache. The source sets no Content-Security-Policy and uses no nonce.

next|GHSA-ggv3-7p47-pfv8.how: Needs a rewrite that proxies to an external backend. next.config.js has no rewrites; the advisory also states hosts that rewrite at the CDN, such as Vercel, are not impacted.

next|GHSA-gx5p-jg67-6x7h.how: Needs a beforeInteractive script carrying untrusted input. The source does not import next/script.

next|GHSA-h27x-g6w4-24gq.how: Needs partial prerendering (experimental.ppr or cacheComponents). Neither is enabled.

next|GHSA-h64f-5h5j-jqjh.how: Self-hosted image optimiser reading a large local image into memory; the advisory states Vercel is not impacted.

next|GHSA-mcj8-r9mp-w47p.how: Needs a root-level catch-all page beside static or ISR routes. The app directory has no catch-all route.

next|GHSA-mq59-m269-xvcx.how: A cross-site request forgery check on Server Actions. The source has no Server Action to forge.

next|GHSA-pc58-hwjq-p385.how: Self-hosted App Router route handlers that return a fetched response unchanged, behind an HTTP/1.1 proxy. The site has no App Router route handler.

next|GHSA-q8wf-6r8g-63ch.how: Self-hosted image optimiser spending CPU on a remote SVG; the advisory states Vercel is not impacted.

next|GHSA-rhh4-g77r-r9qj.how: Needs `use cache` with binary arguments. The source has no `use cache` directive.

next|GHSA-wfc6-r584-vfw7.how: The site serves React Server Component responses, so the vulnerable handling runs. Poisoning needs a shared cache in front that does not separate those responses from HTML. The only cache in front of hooks.gg is Vercel's own; the advisory does not say whether it is affected; see A-2.

next|GHSA-vfv6-92ff-j949.how: Same position as GHSA-wfc6-r584-vfw7: needs a shared cache that mis-partitions Server Component responses; see A-2.

next|GHSA-3g8h-86w9-wvmq.how: Needs a middleware that returns a redirect. The middleware only ever returns NextResponse.next.

next|GHSA-39w2-rjm5-chcv.how: The `next dev` server only; production does not serve the endpoint. It applies to a developer's machine, this box included, while a local dev server runs and a browser there visits a hostile page.

next|GHSA-jcc7-9wpm-mj36.how: The `next dev` server only, and only with allowedDevOrigins configured, which next.config.js does not set.
